The nested class diagram:
**![420](data:image/png;base64,)**

A nested class is essentially a class within a class. It can come in many different forms, and all have unique characteristics. But in each case, it is just a class inside a class.
Here is an example of a standard inner class:
```
public class Foo {
	int a = 1;
	
	public class bar {
		int b = 3;
	}
	
	public int func() {
		return 5;
	}
	
}
```
## Non-Static Inner Class
---
A non-static inner class is the most standard type of inner class. An instance of this type of class must be directly related to an instance of its enclosing class. In other words, you cannot have this type of class without first having an instance of the outer class.
When we make an inner class, it has access to all of the variables of the outer class.
Here is an example:
```
public class Outer {
	private int a = 1;
	private int b;
	
	public Outer(int b) {
		this.b = b;
	}
	
	public class Inner {
		private int c = 3;
		private int d;
		
		public inner(int d) {
			this.d = d;
			System.out.println(a);
		}
	}
}
```
We cannot simply instantiate the inner class from another file. We first need to have an instance of the outer class.
The following is an example of making an instance of the inner class:
```
public class Driver {
	public static void main(String[] args) {
		// First, we instantiate the outer class
		Outer o = new Outer(2);
		
		// Now, we can instantiate the inner class
		Outer.Inner i = o.new Inner(4);
	}
}
```
Notice the strange syntax when we instantiate the inner class.
First, we have to specify `Outer.Inner`, since that is technically the class.
Then, instead of just doing `new`, we use `o.new`. The `new` keyword has to come after the instance, because all inner class instances have to be associated with an instance of an outer class.
Also, this code will print out `1`, since the inner class has access to the variable `a`.
If we wanted to, another way to instantiate the inner class is by doing:
`Outer.Inner i = new Outer(1).new Inner(2);`
## Local Inner Class
---
A method-local inner class is defined within a method, and can only be used inside that method.
This type of inner class cannot have any static variables.
Ex:
```
class Outer {
	void method() {
		class LocalInner {
			void display() {
				System.out.println("Hello");
			}
		}
		LocalInner li = new LocalInner();
		li.display();
	}
}
```
Output:
```
Hello
```

## Anonymous Inner Class
---
Basically a class that is created on the fly. The inner class is not given a name, and it is typically used to quickly implement an interface or abstract class so you can use the abstract methods.
Ex:
```
public interface Greeting {
	void sayHello();
}

public class Driver {
	public static void main(String[] args) {
		Greeting g = new Greeting() {
			public void sayHello() {
				System.out.println("Hello");
			}
		};
		g.sayHello();
	}
}
```
Output:
```
Hello
```
## Static Nested Class
---
Static nested classes act like independent classes that happen to be inside another class. Think of a shed next to a house. The shed is not reliant on the house's existence, it is its own thing. We can make instances of this type of inner class without having an instance of the outer class.
Ex:
```
public class Foo {
	public static class Bar {
		public void function() {
			System.out.println("Hello");
		}	
	}
}

public class Driver {
	public static void main(String[] args) {
		Foo.Bar b = new Foo.Bar();
	}
}
```
We instantiate the inner class in the same style as the non-static inner class, except we don't need an instance of the outer class.

## Examples
Consider the functional inteface:
```
public interface Square {
	public int getArea(int side);
}
```
Use anon class syntax to return the area as the side squared.
```
Square squareOne = new Square() {
	// This is all the anon class
	public int getArea(int side) {
		return side*side;
	}
};
```
